headline: Law lets federal energy regulators give certain hydropower projects up to six more years to start construction.
what_it_does: The law allows the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to extend the deadline to begin building hydropower projects licensed before March 13, 2020. If a license holder asks, FERC can add up to six more years on top of the eight-year extension already allowed under current law. The extra time must be given in no more than three back-to-back two-year periods. FERC may also bring back certain expired licenses for these projects, effective as of the date they expired.

who_it_affects.group: Companies and groups holding older hydropower licenses
who_it_affects.how: Those licensed before March 13, 2020 can ask FERC for up to six extra years to begin construction, and some with expired licenses may have them reinstated.
The agency gains authority to grant these added extensions and to reinstate certain expired licenses.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted May 11, 2026; the summary does not give a separate start date.
